120	of the Infinite One, blessed be He, since He has no body nor form of a body, and "no thought can grasp Him" at all, but rather this is
121	as it is written in the prophet, "By the hand of the prophets I use similitudes." So these likenesses
122	and these revelations are called tzimtzumim, and they are called garments.
123	But without these garments it is impossible to perceive HaShem at all. Without
124	the garments it is impossible; only through garments. And therefore
125	all of Kabbalah is based on this: that all the worlds, the sefirot and the partzufim and so on
126	are really garments and clothing for the supernal lights, so that
127	the lower ones will be able to receive these lights, to receive them at all.
128	Okay?
129	So the Rav writes here: divine perceptions can only be attained through
130	many contractions, from level to level, from a higher intellect to a lower intellect.
131	According to what is explained later in this Torah, higher intellect means Chochmah,
132	and lower intellect is Malchut.
133	In the secret of the sefirot, yes. It is written, "How many are Your works, HaShem,
134	You made them all with wisdom."
135	Our Sages, the Kabbalists, write that...
136	the word "asita," You made, comes from the language of "asiyah," action, and asiyah is like the World of Asiyah, which corresponds to the sefirah of Malchut.
137	And the light of Chochmah is clothed in Malchut, and through this
138	it is revealed in the lower worlds.
139	And so Rabbi Nachman also writes in the first Torah of Likutei Moharan, which is called Torat Ayelet Chen.
140	And so it is written, "How many are Your works, HaShem, You made them all with wisdom."
141	The moment you say the words "wisdom" and "You made," that is the clothing of Chochmah in Malchut.
142	Understood?
143	And here in this Torah we will see that by higher intellect, the Rav means
144	Chochmah, and by lower intellect, Malchut.
145	The Rav writes here: as we see with our senses, that one cannot grasp a great
146	intellect except through its clothing in the lower intellect.
147	The meaning of the words.
148	I want to give a parable for this, my friends, and illustrate it so that it will be understood.
149	The Rav says here, "as we see with our senses."
150	When the Rav says "as we see with our senses," and these are also expressions of our teacher the Ari,
151	"as we see with our senses," or "as we see with the eyes," and so on, they mean,
152	my friends, that you should look at our world,
153	at concepts that you know, and you will understand what I want to tell you.
154	So I will give you an example.
155	Say there is a great rabbi, a great teacher, who is now teaching his student
156	a certain matter, and he sees that the student struggles to understand the concepts.
157	So if he is a good teacher, he knows how to teach, in which way he should teach.
158	He needs to enter the mind of the student, into concepts the student does know,
